correctness.rationale: A unit response using a remote coordinate has limiting c₀ distance equal to max(a(s),a(t)); c₀ vanishing makes this simultaneous for any fixed finite source list. For the reverse bound use source pairs (s,±a(s)e₁). With b the absolute first response coordinate and c the tail supremum, the branch distances are the values of the convex nondecreasing function r↦√((s−t)²+max(r,c)²) at |a(s)−b| and a(s)+b; Jensen and their mean max(a(s),b) give exactly the claimed kernel as a lower bound. A response on e₂ realizes it for these pairs. Equal-weight empirical measures are dense, and continuity is uniform against the compact response set, yielding the attained maximum over measures. Reflection and concavity justify symmetric sources; the resulting response is even. In each variable of K, on either side of the max-switch the normed vector has speed at most one, so the summands are separately 1-Lipschitz, including at zero norm by the reverse triangle inequality. The mesh error is π/(4N), not twice that: rounding a continuous source to the grid bounds one direction; allowing continuous replies against the optimized grid source bounds the other. For thinness a fresh eₙ gives the upper bound and the two scalar poles give the lower bound. For μ₁, averaging replies 0 and 1 yields the strict upper bound by compactness (the two summands cannot attain √2 at the same source radius). For the half-zero/half-poles source, its response function is strictly concave in q=√(1−t²), with equal endpoints. The ±1/√2 perturbation strictly improves both endpoints; continuity gives endpoint neighborhoods and a compact interior gap that persist for a suitably small mixture weight.
residual_risks: Exact error is for the exact LP optimum, not rounded solver digits. The illustrative values were not used as evidence. The review is limited to the stated real space, with no finite-support assertion for the compact game.

value.rationale: The lower index is a natural Banach-space invariant that cannot be read off from thinness. Reducing the infinite-dimensional problem to a single scalar coordinate with matching adversaries gives an exact object usable for optimization, and the uniform finite-LP error makes it computable to a requested precision. The proof identifies a strict mean-versus-worst-case separation in this elementary mixed space rather than merely computing an arbitrary grid example.
residual_risks: No closed form for the limiting value or support classification of its maximizing measure is established.
